findings.comment: Implementations of IAdaptable.getAdapter are expected to return null when an object cannot be adapted, rather than throwing unchecked exceptions. Throwing a RuntimeException will bypass caller null checks (e.g., in DBNPathBase.dropNodes) and abort the entire copy/drop operation if reading a file fails. In addition, the exception e is omitted from log.error, losing the cause and stack trace.
The InputStream returned by node.getAdapter(InputStream.class) is never closed. Neither Files.copy nor this method closes the stream, causing a resource leak.

verdicts.reason: Finding [1] correctly identifies that the InputStream returned from node.getAdapter(InputStream.class) is not closed, causing a resource leak.
None of the automated findings mention the typo/double negative in the log message.
Finding [2] identifies the exact same issue regarding the non-descriptive parameter name 'str' in copyInputStream.
None of the findings mention simplifying the conditional check or using StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING unconditionally.
